theory_refs.at: Fix one, the rest is sorted two-sum

theory_refs.why: Where to skip and why compare with the previous element.

stages.title: Understand
stages.body:
✍️ f(array) → all **unique** triplets [x, y, z] (values, not indices) with x + y + z = 0.
- n ≤ 3000 → O(n²) = 9·10⁶ is fine, O(n³) = 2.7·10¹⁰ is not.
- [−1, 0, 1, 2, −1, −4] → [[−1, −1, 2], [−1, 0, 1]].

stages.title: Analyse
stages.body:
✍️ Target: O(n²). Values are returned, not indices → sorting is allowed.
✍️ By hand: if I fix −1, I need two numbers summing to +1 — that is Two Sum II on the rest of the array.
✍️ Hard part: **unique** triplets. The input [−1, −1, 2] could produce [−1, −1, 2] twice from different −1s.
✍️ Edges: all zeros [0, 0, 0, 0] → one triplet; fewer than 3 elements; no solution.

stages.title: Brainstorm: brute → optimal
stages.body:
✍️ **1. Brute.** Three loops + a set of sorted triplets. O(n³) + dedup overhead.
✍️ ↳ Bottleneck: the inner two loops search for a pair with sum −a[i] — a 2-sum problem.
✍️ **2. Hash per i.** For each i, a hash-set two-sum on the rest. O(n²), but dedup is messy.
✍️ **3. Optimal.** Sort once. For each i: two pointers on i+1..n−1 looking for −a[i]. Dedup by skipping equal values (they are adjacent after sorting). O(n²), O(1) extra.

stages.title: Algorithm in words
stages.body:
✍️ 1. Sort the array.
✍️ 2. For each index i: skip it if a[i] equals a[i−1] (same first value → same triplets). Stop if a[i] > 0.
✍️ 3. Set l = i+1, r = n−1. While l < r: compute the sum. Too small → l++. Too big → r--.
✍️ 4. On a hit: record it, move both pointers, and skip over equal values on both sides.

stages.title: Pseudocode
stages.body:
```
STATE   sort(a); res = []
LOOP    for i in 0..n-3
CHECK     if i > 0 and a[i] == a[i-1]: continue      ← dedup 1
          if a[i] > 0: break
          l = i+1; r = n-1
          while l < r:
              s = a[i] + a[l] + a[r]
              if s < 0: l++
              elif s > 0: r--
              else:
UPDATE            res.add([a[i], a[l], a[r]]); l++; r--
                  while l < r and a[l] == a[l-1]: l++   ← dedup 2
                  while l < r and a[r] == a[r+1]: r--   ← dedup 3
RETURN  res
```

stages.title: Reference C++
Edge cases and complexity
stages.body:
✍️ O(n²) time, O(1) extra (besides output and the sort).
✍️ Skipping on `a[i] == a[i+1]` (instead of `a[i−1]`) would skip the **first** −1 and lose [−1, −1, 2].
- [0, 0, 0, 0]: i = 0 finds [0, 0, 0]; the inner skips and i = 1.. are duplicates.

stages.title: Carry forward
stages.body:
✍️ k-sum → sort + fix k−2 elements + two pointers → O(n^(k−1)).
✍️ "Unique combinations of values" → sort, then skip equal neighbours instead of using a set.
✍️ Fixing one element turns an unfamiliar problem into a familiar one — a general strategy.

stages.title: Interview follow-ups
stages.body:
- *3Sum Closest* — same scan, track the best |sum − target|.
- *4Sum* — two outer loops + two pointers, `long long` sums.
- *Count triplets with sum < target* — when the sum is small enough, add r − l at once.
- *Can it be done in better than O(n²)?* Not in general (3SUM is believed to need ~n²); say so.

siblings.title: 3Sum Closest
siblings.maps: Same sorted scan, but instead of an exact hit you track the sum nearest the target.

stages.title: Analyse
stages.body: ✍️ Return the sum of three numbers closest to target (one answer).

stages.title: Brainstorm
stages.body: ✍️ Brute O(n³). Sort + fix i + two pointers: the pointer moves are the same (too small → l++, too big → r−−); record whichever sum has the smallest |s − target|. No dedup needed.

stages.title: Algorithm in words
stages.body: ✍️ Sort; for each i, scan with l and r, updating the best sum; return early on an exact match.

stages.title: Pseudocode
stages.body:
```
sort a; best = a[0]+a[1]+a[2]
for i: l = i+1; r = n-1
    while l < r:
        s = a[i]+a[l]+a[r]
        if |s-t| < |best-t|: best = s
        if s < t: l++ elif s > t: r-- else: return s
return best
```

stages.title: Reference C++
Quick theory
stages.body: ✍️ "Closest" versions keep the pointer logic and add a running best ([[tp-fix-one-k-sum#variations]]).

siblings.title: 4Sum
siblings.maps: One more fixed loop; dedup at both fixed levels; `long long` sums.

stages.title: Analyse
stages.body: ✍️ All unique quadruplets summing to target; values up to 10⁹ → sums overflow int.

stages.title: Brainstorm
stages.body: ✍️ Sort; fix i and j (both with dedup); two pointers for the last two. O(n³).

stages.title: Algorithm in words
stages.body: ✍️ Two outer loops with "skip equal to previous at this level", inner two-pointer scan with dedup after hits.

stages.title: Pseudocode
stages.body:
```
for i: skip dup; for j > i: skip dup (j > i+1)
    l = j+1; r = n-1; two-pointer on long long sum
```

stages.title: Reference C++
Quick theory
stages.body: ✍️ Dedup guard at a nested level is `j > i + 1`, the start of that level ([[tp-skip-duplicates#pitfalls]]).

siblings.title: Valid Triangle Number
siblings.maps: Fix the largest side; on the rest, two pointers count a block of valid pairs at once.

stages.title: Analyse
stages.body: ✍️ Count triples that can form a triangle: for sorted a ≤ b ≤ c, need a + b > c.

stages.title: Brainstorm
stages.body: ✍️ Sort. For each c = a[k] (from the right), l = 0, r = k−1: if a[l] + a[r] > a[k], every l' in [l, r−1] also works with r → add r − l, r−−; else l++. O(n²).

stages.title: Algorithm in words
stages.body: ✍️ Fix the largest side, count pairs on its left with the block trick.

stages.title: Pseudocode
stages.body:
```
sort a; cnt = 0
for k from n-1 down to 2:
    l = 0; r = k-1
    while l < r:
        if a[l] + a[r] > a[k]: cnt += r - l; r--
        else: l++
```

stages.title: Reference C++
Quick theory
stages.body: ✍️ Fixing the **largest** element makes the condition a single inequality — choose what to fix so the rest is a known 2-pointer problem.
